title: Family Systems Therapy
welcome: Every child brings a whole family into the room, visibly or not. This course teaches you to see and work with that system.
vignette: A ten-year-old's stomachaches vanish on weekends and return on school mornings. The pediatrician finds nothing. In session, the parents sit on opposite edges of the couch. The symptom, you begin to suspect, is speaking for the family.
vignette_attr: A family intake, drawn from supervised practice
description: A systemic study of the family as the unit of treatment: systems theory and family structure, Bowen and structural and strategic approaches, communication patterns, the family life cycle, and conducting conjoint sessions with children and their caregivers.
questions: How do I join a whole family at once?
How is change made in a system that resists it?
importance: Most child symptoms are embedded in family patterns
Family involvement is the strongest predictor of lasting change
Systems thinking prevents blaming the identified patient
misconceptions: that family therapy means seeing everyone every session, when the system can be worked through parts
that the child's diagnosis is the target, when the pattern is often the target
figures: whose differentiation and triangles mapped the emotional system
whose structural therapy reorganized family hierarchies
who brought communication and warmth to systems work
outcomes: You will see boundaries, hierarchies, and triangles in live interaction.
Apply Bowen, structural, and strategic models
You will choose and use systemic frameworks with precision.
Join and hold a whole family
You will build alliance across generations in one room.
You will relocate the problem from child to pattern without blame.
You will craft enactments and tasks that shift the system.
You will match interventions to the family's developmental stage.
modules: Systems Thinking and the Identified Patient
The shift from linear to circular is the course's core move.
Bowen gives you a map across generations.
Minuchin teaches you to act in the room, not just talk.
Strategic work targets the pattern that keeps the problem alive.
Many symptoms mark a transition the family cannot navigate.
Conjoint Sessions with Children and Caregivers
The conjoint session is where systemic skill becomes visible.
Ethics, Culture and the Systemic Counselor
The therapist's own family of origin
The systemic counselor must see their own system too.
practicum: Practice uses live and recorded families.
Genogram construction of your own family
assessment: A genogram and structural case formulation
A recorded conjoint segment with critique
tips: Draw the family before you treat it; the map reveals the move
Keep the child's voice audible in the system
integration: Family systems thinking reframes every child course in this programme.
faith: The family is the first community; we honor it even as we help it change.
closing: May you see the whole family with compassion, and may the child in the middle finally be free.
